title: Turnitin AI writing detection bias against non-native English speakers
system_purpose: Detect AI-generated text in student essays to flag potential academic dishonesty
decision_impact: Students flagged as cheaters face failing grades and disciplinary hearings affecting academic standing
verified_facts: Stanford researchers empirically tested 7 commercial AI detectors and found systematic bias: detectors misclassified non-native English writing as AI-generated at dramatically higher rates than native English writing due to lower text perplexity.
reported_harm: Academic opportunity loss and discriminatory false cheating accusations leading to failing grades and delayed graduation and psychological distress for non-native English speakers.
quantitative_evidence: 61.3 percent of TOEFL essays by non-native speakers were misclassified as AI-generated; 97.8 percent were flagged by at least one detector; Vanderbilt University identified approximately 4 percent baseline false positive rate.
limitations: Turnitin continuously updates its models; the Stanford study tested specific detector versions on specific essay corpora and results may not generalize to all current detection products.

title: NEDA Tessa chatbot harmful advice to eating disorder patients
system_purpose: Provide educational support and prevention information about eating disorders to help-seekers
decision_impact: Chatbot advice directly influenced vulnerable users health decisions and replaced trained human crisis support staff
affected_groups: eating disorder patients;vulnerable youth;crisis helpline workers
verified_facts: NEDA replaced its 20-year human crisis helpline with AI chatbot Tessa after staff voted to unionize. Within days of launch clinical experts documented that Tessa dispensed dangerous weight-loss advice to users seeking help for active eating disorders. NEDA pulled the bot offline on 2023-05-30.
reported_harm: Potentially life-threatening health advice to people with active eating disorders including recommending daily calorie deficits and food tracking with restrictive apps.
quantitative_evidence: The human helpline previously handled approximately 70000 crisis contacts per year; the chatbot explicitly advised maintaining a daily calorie deficit of 500 to 1000 calories to users with active eating disorders.
limitations: Tessa was originally a validated rule-based CBT prevention tool; the harmful behavior occurred after commercialization and modification without adequate guardrails; limited independent technical audit was published.

title: Character.AI teen psychological harm and student disengagement
system_purpose: Provide AI conversational companions for entertainment and learning support to users including minors
decision_impact: Prolonged unmonitored AI interaction influenced vulnerable adolescent emotional state and school engagement
verified_facts: The Garcia v. Character Technologies lawsuit alleged that a 14-year-old student developed severe emotional dependence on an AI chatbot over months. Court filings documented daily chat logs showing progressive school disengagement and isolation. The platform lacked minor safety barriers and crisis safeguards.
reported_harm: Psychological dependence and school disengagement leading to a reported death by suicide of a 14-year-old student who used the chatbot without parental awareness or escalation safeguards.
quantitative_evidence: Character.AI reported over 20 million active users with adolescents averaging approximately 2 hours per day; court filings documented thousands of pages of unmonitored chat logs.
limitations: The case settled before trial so allegations were not adjudicated; adolescent suicide involves multifaceted mental health vulnerabilities making AI a contributory rather than sole causal factor.
